definitions.gloss: to brace oneself, to prepare oneself (physically)
definitions.explanation: To take a defensive or ready posture in preparation for something. Often used in martial arts or physical confrontation contexts.

definitions.gloss: to be on guard, to tense up (psychologically)
definitions.explanation: To mentally prepare for something or to become tense/defensive in anticipation. Can imply excessive caution.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}に{対|たい}して{身構|みがま}える
examples.english: to brace oneself against an enemy

examples.japanese: {拳|こぶし}を{握|にぎ}って{身構|みがま}えた。
examples.english: He clenched his fists and braced himself.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}が{来|き}ると{思|おも}って{身構|みがま}えたが、{何|なに}も{起|お}きなかった。
examples.english: I braced myself thinking an earthquake was coming, but nothing happened.

examples.japanese: そんなに{身構|みがま}えないで。
{初対面|しょたいめん}の{人|ひと}と{話|はな}すとき、つい{身構|みがま}えてしまう。
examples.english: When talking to someone for the first time, I tend to tense up.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{面接|めんせつ}で{身構|みがま}えすぎて、{緊張|きんちょう}が{伝|つた}わってしまった。
examples.english: She was too tense in the interview, and her nervousness showed.

notes:
FORMATION: Compound of {身|み} (body) + {構|かま}える (to set up, take a stance).

TRANSITIVITY: Intransitive ({自動詞|じどうし}).

CONJUGATION: Ichidan verb: {身構|みがま}えない, {身構|みがま}えます, {身構|みがま}えて.

USAGE: Often used in the negative sense of being too tense or overly defensive. {身構|みがま}えすぎる (to be too on guard) is a common pattern.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {身構|みがま}える{必要|ひつよう}はない (no need to be on guard)
- {身構|みがま}えすぎる (to be too tense/defensive)
- ～に{対|たい}して{身構|みがま}える (to brace against ~)

RELATED WORDS:
- {構|かま}える (to take a stance - base verb)
- {警戒|けいかい}する (to be on guard - more formal)
- {緊張|きんちょう}する (to be nervous/tense)
